descriptionChirho: To swear an oath or make a solemn vow, binding oneself by invoking a higher authority. Encompasses all tense/aspect forms of the verb: Jesus' teaching against swearing oaths (Matt 5:34, 36), the discourse on what one swears by (Matt 23:16-22), Peter's denial under oath (Matt 26:74; Mark 14:71), God's oath to Abraham (Luke 1:73; Acts 2:30; Heb 6:13, 16), God swearing in wrath (Heb 3:11, 18; 4:3), the Melchizedek priesthood oath (Heb 7:21), the angel's oath in Revelation (Rev 10:6), and the prohibition against swearing (Jas 5:12). All multilingual glosses converge: Arabic aqsama/halafa, German schworen, French jurer, Hebrew nishba/lehishavea, Hindi shapath khana/kasam khana, Korean maengsehada, Spanish jurar.
